A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EgoBrain and Brain-TIM. All 21 pages of v1 and 22 pages of v2, including equations, tables, figures and appendices, support comparison. The appendix visualizations can be matched despite renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original action-recognition experiments, component ablations, confusion matrices and success/failure cases on the collected EgoBrain dataset in Tables 1–2 and Figures 4–5.

after.justification: v2 retains original EgoBrain experiments and analyses, including revised cross-subject recognition results in Table 1 and the retained component ablations in Table 2.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Appendix A retain Brain-TIM's feature encoders, temporal and modality embeddings, transformer, classification heads and weighted cross-entropy objective. Removing the spatial-fusion comparator and adding preprocessing documentation do not establish a change to the proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 61-hour dataset from 40 participants, covering 29 actions and 10 verbs, with cross-subject-only and cross-subject/cross-scene evaluation. The pretraining sources and appendix participant/action examples are also retained.

E2.justification: v2 removes Table 1's Spatial fusion comparator from both evaluation protocols while retaining brain-only and visual-only comparisons. VideoMAE and LaBraM are newly named in the table but were already documented in v1 Appendix A.1; they are not added baselines.

E3.justification: Table 1's caption changes from validation-set, within-scene evaluation to test-set evaluation under both protocols. Since v1's surrounding text already says test sets, this is a reported protocol clarification rather than evidence of rerunning experiments. Section 3's participant splits and the Top-1 metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 removes the temporal-versus-spatial fusion ablation and its supporting comparison from Section 5.2 and Table 1. Table 2's component ablations, Figure 4's confusion matrices and Figure 5's success/failure cases remain unchanged. The added parameter counts do not constitute a capacity-matched control experiment.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations across five random seeds. v2 repeats this information in Table 1's caption but introduces no new uncertainty-estimation procedure, confidence interval or significance test. Its new statistically significant wording does not document such a test.

E6.justification: The main cross-subject result block is substantially revised. Table 1's verb/action means change from 23.19/12.12 to 21.53/8.44 for EEG, 92.50/82.80 to 88.95/78.44 for vision, and 92.72/84.48 to 90.11/80.16 for Brain-TIM; their standard deviations also change. Spatial-fusion results disappear. Retained cross-scene results, Table 2 and Figures 4–5 are unchanged. Given v1's conflicting validation/test descriptions, these are revised reported results, not established same-setting performance losses.

T1.justification: Removing the spatial-fusion subsection also removes its explicit mathematical definition of the concatenated input sequence with shape (N+Q) × 3D. The task formulation, Brain-TIM sequence construction, token definitions and loss equations remain. Neither version contains additional theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same dataset novelty claim, Brain-TIM contribution and claim of complementary EEG–vision information. The headline 66.70% action-recognition result and the stated dataset scale are unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds an interpretation that EEG's gains reflect unique cognitive information rather than model capacity, based on its comparatively small parameter count. It removes the temporal-versus-spatial superiority interpretation and the Broader Impacts discussion of specific applications and neural-data privacy. Existing category-dependent benefits and failure explanations remain.

D1.justification: New Appendix B specifies 0.1–75 Hz filtering, a 50 Hz notch, 200 Hz resampling, amplitude scaling, channel removal and EDF-to-HDF5 conversion. Table 1 adds parameter counts of 5.8M, 305.0M and 310.8M; Appendix A.1 shortens LaBraM-Base to LaBraM. These expand or revise documentation without establishing an implementation change. The relationship between Appendix B's filtering and the retained 0.5–50 Hz specification in Appendix A.2 is unexplained.

R1.justification: The same 41 cited works and substantive positioning relative to EEG research, egocentric datasets and TIM are retained. Author–year citations, alphabetical reference ordering and added bibliographic metadata do not introduce new related work.

P1.justification: Section 5.1 is locally rewritten, correcting reversed verb/action attribution and the assignment of multimodal scores to vision alone. Section 5.2 is shortened, Broader Impacts is removed, and the new preprocessing appendix shifts More Visualization from B to C. Most narrative and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 1 is redesigned from protocol column groups into protocol row blocks, replacing Fusion with Encoder and adding Params. The title, headings, running headers, bibliography and spacing are restyled. Table 2 and figure content remain; appendix Figures S1–S7 become Figures 6–12 and are repositioned.

improvement.justification: v2 improves reporting clarity through corrected Table 1 labels and score attribution, parameter counts and explicit preprocessing details. However, removing the spatial-fusion comparison weakens evidence for Brain-TIM's fusion choice, while the new capacity-independent and statistically significant interpretations lack corresponding controls or tests. Unexplained cross-subject result replacements and unreconciled filtering descriptions further limit confidence. These benefits and harms do not support a reliable net-quality judgment.
